_about: The two courses. Each models a public range. plates lists each steel plate: its distance, its width and height in inches, how high it stands above the firing line (riseFt, its own figure, used by the engine and the drawing alike) and where it stands sideways (lateralYd, placed by angle as seen from the firing line). altitudeFt is the range's height above sea level, for the air. blurb is the one line home shows about the course.

cta-piru.name: Canyon course (modeled on California Tactical Academy, Piru)

source.note: the range's own contact page; it adds that it was previously known as Wes Thompson's Piru Rifle Range. read from the search engine's indexed text of this page on the date given: this session's network allowed web search but no page fetches

"Steel targets are set from 100 yards all the way up to 1000 yards"; https://ctala.com/the-ultimate-guide-to-1000-yard-rifle-ranges-in-california-why-cta-stands-out/ says paper 50 to 400 yards and steel 100 to 1,000 yards. read from the search engine's indexed text of this page on the date given: this session's network allowed web search but no page fetches

altitudeFt.estimate: no elevation service could be reached from this session. Holser Canyon is listed at 830 ft at the canyon (USGS Piru quadrangle via https://www.topozone.com/?p=750134) and the town of Piru at 709 ft (https://www.topozone.com/?p=661862); the range is about 1.5 miles up the canyon road, so 850 ft

lateralYd.estimate: where the plate stands sideways, in yards, from the line straight downrange: the range publishes no layout; the plates are placed by their angle as seen from the firing line, -108 minutes of angle (nearest on the left, each farther plate 27 minutes of angle further right), so no two share a spot and the order reads across the hillside

source.note: steel every 100 yards from 100 to 1,000. read from the search engine's indexed text of this page on the date given: this session's network allowed web search but no page fetches

widthIn.estimate: the range publishes no plate sizes; 12 by 18 in plates to 500 yards, 18 by 24 to 800, 24 by 36 beyond are common steel sizes

heightIn.estimate: same basis: the same basis as the figure next to it in this entry

riseFt.estimate: how high the plate stands above the firing line, in feet: the brief puts the far plates on a slope "that rises to maybe a couple hundred feet", so the 1,000-yard plate is 200 ft up (range-day-one brief) and the others follow a slope that steepens with distance, 200 × (yards / 1000)^1.6, so each farther plate sits visibly higher in the view than the one before it (the steps are 14 to 25 minutes of angle). An estimate until photographs of the range decide it

angeles-sylmar.name: Rifle line (modeled on Angeles Shooting Ranges, Sylmar)

address.value: 12651 Little Tujunga Canyon Road, Sylmar (Lake View Terrace), CA 91342

source.note: the range's own services page did not show the street address in the indexed text; third-party listings give it, with the city as Lake View Terrace. read from the search engine's indexed text of this page on the date given: this session's network allowed web search but no page fetches

berms at 100, 200, 300, 400, 500 and 600 yards; steel at 600; paper to 200 yards on weekends and 300 on weekdays; 100-yard targets at the benches. read from the search engine's indexed text of this page on the date given: this session's network allowed web search but no page fetches

altitudeFt.estimate: no elevation service could be reached from this session. Sylmar is about 1,270 ft (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylmar,_Los_Angeles) and the range sits up Little Tujunga Canyon above the town; 1,500 ft

lateralYd.estimate: where the plate stands sideways, in yards, from the line straight downrange: the range publishes no layout; one visitor's description puts the 500 and 600 yard targets a little to the left of the rifle side (https://www.pewpewtactical.com/review-of-angeles-shooting-range-sylmar-ca/), so the plates run from the nearest on the right to the farthest on the left, each 30 minutes of angle further left as seen from the firing line (this plate at 75)

riseFt.estimate: how high the plate stands above the firing line, in feet: nothing published describes how the ground runs toward the 600-yard berm (the range's own pages name only the berm distances), so a gentle rise is used, 1 ft at 100 yards growing as the square of the distance to 36 ft at 600 (about 1 degree at the far berm), which puts each farther plate 11 minutes of angle higher in the view than the one before it.
